title: Understanding the Minimum Wage Australia 17 Year Old Rate: Hourly to Annual Conversion
description: Learn how to convert the minimum wage Australia 17 year old rate to annual pay, including tax, super, and fortnightly earnings. Use our timesheet for accurate estimates.
salarySummary: For a 17-year-old on the National Minimum Wage (junior rate), annual gross pay is hourly rate × hours per week × 52, assuming 38 hours per week, but the exact junior rate depends on the applicable award.

faqs.q: What is the minimum wage for a 17-year-old in Australia?
faqs.a: The minimum wage for a 17-year-old is not a single figure; it is a junior rate set as a percentage of the adult National Minimum Wage. The percentage depends on the award or registered agreement that covers the job. For example, under the Miscellaneous Award, a 17-year-old may receive a lower percentage than an adult, but you must check the specific award or use the Fair Work Ombudsman's Pay Calculator for the exact rate.

faqs.q: How do I calculate annual pay from my hourly rate as a 17-year-old?
faqs.a: To estimate annual gross pay, multiply your hourly rate by the number of hours you work per week, then multiply by 52. For a standard full-time week of 38 hours, the formula is: hourly rate × 38 × 52. Remember that this assumes no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, or allowances. For a casual employee, add 25% casual loading on top of the base rate before calculating. Use our timesheet for a quick estimate.

faqs.q: Does superannuation get paid on top of my hourly rate?
faqs.a: Yes, superannuation (super) is paid on top of your ordinary earnings. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, and it is not deducted from your hourly rate. For example, if your hourly rate is $20, your employer must contribute an additional $2.40 per hour into your super fund, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This applies to both adult and junior employees.

bodyMarkdown:
## How to Convert Your Hourly Rate to Annual Pay

If you earn an hourly wage, you can estimate your annual gross pay using a simple formula: **hourly rate × hours per week × 52**. This assumes you work the same number of hours every week, with no unpaid overtime, penalty rates, allowances, or salary sacrifice. For a standard full-time week, we assume 38 hours, as set by the Fair Work Ombudsman. For example, if you are on the **minimum wage australia 17 year old** junior rate, you would multiply that rate by 38 and then by 52 to get your annual gross.

To find your fortnightly pay, simply double your weekly pay: **weekly pay × 2**. This can help with budgeting if you are paid every two weeks. Remember that these are gross figures before tax and other deductions.

## National Minimum Wage vs Award Rates

The National Minimum Wage is the legal minimum for employees not covered by an award or agreement. From 1 July 2026, the adult rate is $26.44 per hour, or $1004.90 per week for 38 hours. However, most employees are covered by an award that sets higher minimum rates for their industry or role. For a **minimum wage australia 17 year old**, junior rates apply. These are a percentage of the adult rate, determined by the Fair Work Commission. The exact percentage varies by award – for instance, under the Miscellaneous Award, a 17-year-old may receive 60% of the adult rate, but you should check the specific award for your job. The Fair Work Ombudsman provides a Pay Calculator to find the correct rate.

If you are a casual employee, you are entitled to a 25% casual loading on top of your base hourly rate. This loading compensates for not receiving paid leave. When using our [the timesheet](/) calculator, you can check a box to add the 25% loading automatically. Do not type a rate that already includes casual loading; always start with the base rate.

## Superannuation Paid on Top

Superannuation (super) is an additional payment your employer must make into a super fund on your behalf. The super guarantee rate is 12% of your ordinary time earnings, and it is paid **on top** of your hourly rate. For example, if your hourly rate is $20, your employer contributes an extra $2.40 per hour, up to the maximum contribution base of $270,830 per year. This applies to both adult and junior employees, including those on the **minimum wage australia 17 year old** rate. Super is not deducted from your pay; it is an extra cost to the employer.

## Tax and Take-Home Pay

Your take-home pay is your gross pay minus tax and the Medicare levy. For the 2026–27 financial year, the resident tax rates are:

- Nil on income up to $18,200
- 15% on income from $18,201 to $45,000
- 30% on income from $45,001 to $135,000
- 37% on income from $135,001 to $190,000
- 45% on income above $190,000

Additionally, the Medicare levy is generally 2% of your taxable income. The Australian Taxation Office uses these rates to calculate your tax. For a junior employee on the **minimum wage australia 17 year old** rate, your annual income may be below the tax-free threshold, meaning you may not pay any tax. However, if you earn more, the progressive rates apply.

Use our [minimum wage](/topics/minimum-wage) page for more details on the National Minimum Wage and junior rates. For a full breakdown of tax and super, see our [take-home pay](/topics/take-home) guide.

## Disclaimer

Annual pay here is hourly rate × hours per week × 52. It assumes the same rate every week, no unpaid overtime, no penalty rates, no allowances, and no salary sacrifice. Super is estimated at 12% of ordinary earnings only, paid on top, and stops at the $270,830 maximum contribution base. Tax is the 2026–27 resident scale with the full tax-free threshold. Medicare uses the 2025–26 single reduction thresholds because the 2026–27 reduction thresholds were not confirmed here. HELP, the Medicare levy surcharge, and salary packaging are not deducted. This is an estimate, not a determination of your pay or tax.
